plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant blossoms open on bare branches while winter's chill still lingers. The delicate, spicy-sweet flowers cover gnarled trees in drifts of blush and white. They are celebrated in ume festivals across Japan's gardens and orchards.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to mid-March, peaking in late February and early March
plants.location: Japan, including Kyoto, Mito and the Tokyo region
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms signal the end of winter in East Asian culture, and the tree's fruit is pickled into the tangy umeboshi.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding trumpets of golden yellow rise above ribbon-like leaves, lighting up woodland edges and meadows. In sheltered spots they form sunlit carpets that announce the arrival of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to April, with peak bloom commonly in March
plants.location: Western Europe, including southern England, Wales and the Gloucestershire daffodil woods
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain toxic alkaloids. One of them, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: Leafless stems shoot up in the late summer warmth and carry clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. The blooms seem to appear from bare ground, which gives the plant its nickname.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly February to April
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa, and naturalised in southern Australia
plants.funFact: The flowers emerge long after the leaves have died back, so the bulb survives dry summers underground and then flowers in a sudden burst.
